Quick Read

Micron (MU) faces direct CXMT competition since every dollar comes from memory, while Intel (INTC) could actually benefit if Chinese supply drives down DRAM costs.

Micron's 26 take-or-pay contracts lock in over 35% of revenue through 2030, buffering near-term CXMT pricing pressure alongside its unmatched HBM lead.

CXMT's denser 4F square server DRAM launches before end of 2026, targeting a market where DRAM prices already surged high-teens percent.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) both posted AI-fueled quarters. Now both face the same question from China. CXMT, also known as ChangXin Memory Technologies, says it will launch a new server memory product before the end of 2026 using a denser 4F square design. Micron sells memory. Intel buys it. That one difference shapes who should worry more.

24/7 Wall St.
Tight Memory Supply Pays Micron and Pinches Intel's PCs

Micron's fiscal Q4 revenue reached $54.23B, up 379.3% YoY, with non-GAAP gross margin of 87.0%. Margins like that only happen when sellers set the price. DRAM brought in $39.8 billion, or 73% of total revenue, and DRAM prices rose in the high teens percentage range. CXMT's added capacity takes aim at exactly that pricing.

Intel's Q2 revenue rose 25.4% YoY to $16.13B, powered by Data Center and AI growth of 59%. For Intel, memory is a cost. Management expects PC consumption to fall "low double digits percent for all of 2026, impacted by rising memory prices and constraints."

Micron Leans on Contracts While Intel Could Gain From Cheaper Chips

Micron has signed 26 Strategic Customer Agreements covering over 35% of revenue through 2030, all with take-or-pay volumes. That protects demand, though the remaining quarter of expected SCA revenue still reprices against market rates. HBM4 is in high-volume shipments, and HBM4E on 1-gamma targets calendar 2027 production. CXMT has yet to match those leading-edge products. Still, the earnings call never mentioned CXMT by name, which leaves investors wondering about how management views the threat.

Intel (INTC) posted its strongest revenue growth in 15 years, with Data Center and AI revenue up 59% and EPS nearly doubling consensus.

Qualcomm's automotive revenue hit a record $1.6 billion, rising 61%, as two new hyperscaler custom chip wins begin generating revenue this December.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

For the first period of the AI build-out, investors poured into GPU makers. Now spending is moving toward custom silicon, optical connectivity, inference CPUs and edge devices, and three chipmakers sit right in that path.

Thongden Studio / Shutterstock.com

Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) is up 168.54% year to date. Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) is up 143.5%, and Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) has gained 2.21%. Last week Marvell fell 17.24% and Intel dropped 14.18%, so all three start 2027 from a lower base. Here's how each could reach a bold target next year.

The spending shift reaches well beyond silicon, into the power, cooling, and networking that feed every new data center (our free report profiles seven of those non-chipmaker suppliers: 7 Stocks Powering the AI Boom (That Aren't Chipmakers)).

Marvell Can Hit $350 in 2027 if Custom Silicon Delivers

Data center now makes up 79% of Marvell's revenue, and that business grew 46% last quarter. CEO Matt Murphy said custom silicon "will more than double year over year in fiscal 2028." An expanded hyperscaler agreement includes a warrant for up to 7% of Marvell's shares, linked to revenue milestones.

At $227.83, MRVL trades at 31x the fiscal 2028 EPS estimate of $7.2963. Reaching $350 would be a 54% gain and put the stock at 48x earnings. That's a premium, but analysts expect 73% EPS growth, and 90 days ago the estimate was only $6.1994. What might drive Marvell to $350?

What Happened?

JPMorgan upgraded Intel (INTC:NASDAQ) to Neutral from Underweight late Friday, according to Investing.com. Intel stock gained nearly 3% on Monday, following the upgrade.

The firm said the risk and reward now look more balanced even as Intel stock trades above JPMorgan's $85 price target. However, the tech stock is also down about 36% from its June peak.

Analyst Harlan Sur said the turnaround will take years. But he said management has made a solid start and his confidence in the recovery is rising, while pointing to AI-related demand as a tailwind.

The upgrade fits what Intel showed on its Q2 call. Revenue was $16.1 billion, which was $1.8 billion above the midpoint of guidance. EPS of $0.42 beat the $0.20 guide by a wide margin.

CEO Lip-Bu Tan said it was the seventh straight quarter of beating expectations.

INTC Stock Revenue, EBIT and Free Cash Flow Estimates in Billion USD (TIKR)

Data center was the key driver as revenue rose 59% from last year. Intel also said its AI-driven businesses grew more than 70% and made up about 70% of revenue.

Manufacturing is improving too. Output on Intel 18A was about 25% above target and management said yields are tracking ahead of plan.

What the Market Is Telling Us About Intel Stock

For Intel stock, the upgrade is a cautious vote of confidence, not a cheer. Neutral means JPMorgan sees fewer reasons to be bearish and does not call Intel a bargain.

There are real risks. Intel said supply is still tight and it expects PC demand to fall by a low double-digit percentage in 2026.

It also plans to spend more than $20 billion on capital in 2026, with a bigger number in 2027. CFO David Zinsner said that could weigh on cash flow next year.

Intel stock now depends on turning demand into supply.

Management said it will fall short of demand again in Q4, even as supply improves.
